title: Design the API edge
intro: REST at the boundary, gRPC on the hot paths inside — now wire it.
briefing: A public mobile app must place orders, which requires a payment check on every order (a hot internal path). Third-party clients never see your internal services — everything public enters through the REST gateway.

rules.label: Public traffic enters via the REST gateway
No public client calls Orders directly
No public client calls Payments directly
The gateway routes order requests inside
Orders ↔ Payments: the internal gRPC hot path
An order can actually reach the payment check

debrief: The edge is REST because public clients are many, unknown, and long-lived: they need a stateless, cacheable, loosely-coupled contract that can evolve behind a versioned gateway. Inside, Orders → Payments runs on every order — a latency-critical call between two services YOU own and deploy together, which is exactly where gRPC's binary protobuf + strongly-typed contract pays. The rule of thumb you just wired: REST at the boundary, RPC between your own services, and nothing internal ever exposed directly to the public.
